title: Real conversation
goal: Tell a friend what happened, react to their news, pass on what someone said, and keep a chat going with the little words Kannadigas really use.
intro:
This unit is about conversation itself: telling a friend what happened at work or on the way home, gasping at their news, passing on gossip, and keeping the chat going. Kannadigas call a long, easy chat **ಹರಟೆ** (*haraṭe*), and a good one happens over coffee at a darshini or on the steps outside someone's house.

You'll learn the reactions (**ಹೌದಾ?** 'really?', **ಅಯ್ಯೋ ಪಾಪ!** 'oh, poor thing!', **ತಮಾಷೆ ಮಾಡ್ತಿದ್ದೀಯಾ?** 'are you kidding?'), the fillers (**ಅಂದ್ರೆ, ಏನಂದ್ರೆ, ಗೊತ್ತಾ?, ಅಲ್ವಾ?**), how to report what someone said with **ಅಂತ**, gossip with **-ಅಂತೆ** 'apparently', and the **relative participles** that give you 'the film I saw' and 'what you said' with no word for 'who' or 'which'.

With friends your age you'll use **ನೀನು**, so most of this unit is in ನೀನು forms (ಹೇಳು, ಮಾಡ್ತಿದ್ದೀಯಾ, ಅಂದೆ); use ನೀವು with anyone older or anyone you don't know well.

vocab.note: ಏನು ಸುದ್ದಿ? 'What's new?' Also ಏನ್ ಸಮಾಚಾರ? 'what's the news?'
ಏನು ವಿಷಯ? 'What's up? What's it about?' ಅದು ಬೇರೆ ವಿಷಯ 'that's another matter'.
ಅವನ ಮಾತು ನಂಬಬೇಡ 'don't trust what he says'. ಮಾತು ಕೊಡು 'give one's word, promise'.
Formal spelling ಕಥೆ kathe. ಅವನ ಕತೆ ಬಿಡು 'forget about him'.
ಹರಟೆ ಹೊಡೆ 'to chat, shoot the breeze' (past ಹೊಡೆದ್ವಿ 'we chatted').

vocab.en: to say (in quotes and short reports)
vocab.note: Spoken past: ಅಂದೆ 'I said', ಅಂದ 'he said', ಅಂದ್ಳು 'she said', ಅಂದ್ರು 'they said'. Present ಅಂತಾರೆ 'they say, it's called'. ಅಂತ comes from this verb.

vocab.en: to come to know, find out; to understand
vocab.note: Used with the dative: ನನಗೆ ತಿಳೀತು 'I found out'. ತಿಳಿಸು 'to inform, let someone know'.
ನಂಬೋಕೆ ಆಗ್ತಿಲ್ಲ 'I can't believe it'. Spoken present ನಂಬ್ತೀನಿ.

vocab.en: to scold, tell off; to swear at
vocab.note: The person scolded is in the dative: ನನಗೆ ಬೈದ್ರು 'they told me off'. Past ಬೈದ-, present ಬೈತಾರೆ.
ಗಲಾಟೆ ಮಾಡಬೇಡಿ 'don't make noise'. Also used for a public row.
ತಮಾಷೆ ಮಾಡು 'to joke, tease'; ತಮಾಷೆಗೆ 'for fun, as a joke'.
From English. ನನಗೆ ಶಾಕ್ ಆಯ್ತು 'I was shocked'.
ಅಯ್ಯೋ ದೇವರೇ! 'oh my God!'
Literally 'sin'. ಪಾಪ, ಅವನಿಗೆ ಹುಷಾರಿಲ್ಲ 'poor guy, he's not well'.
Spoken ಸುಮ್ನೆ summne. ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ ಕೇಳಿದೆ 'I was just asking'; ಸುಮ್ಮನಿರು 'be quiet, keep out of it'.
Spoken also ಇದ್ದಕ್ಕಿದ್ದ ಹಾಗೆ iddakkidda hāge.
Literally 'within that much (time)'.
ಹೇಗೆ 'how' + -ಓ 'some-': like ಏನೋ 'something', ಯಾರೋ 'someone'.

vocab.en: I mean, that is; so you mean...
vocab.note: Spoken ಅಂದ್ರೆ andre. Literally 'if (you) say'.
Starts an explanation. Careful form ಏನೆಂದರೆ.
Fused to the end of a sentence: ಬರ್ತಾನಂತೆ 'apparently he's coming'.

vocab.en: right?, isn't it?, don't you think?
vocab.note: Careful form ಅಲ್ಲವಾ / ಅಲ್ಲವೇ. Also fused: ಇದ್ದಾರಲ್ವಾ 'they're there, right?'
Spoken also ನಿಜವಾಗ್ಲೂ.

vocab.en: anyway, in short, all in all
vocab.note: Wraps up a story.
Changes the topic.
ಯಾರು 'who' + -ಓ. 'Anyone' in questions is ಯಾರಾದ್ರೂ.
ಏನು 'what' + -ಓ. ಏನೋ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ 'I don't really know'.
ಅದು + emphatic -ಏ. ಅದೇ! 'Exactly!'
After the genitive: ನಿನ್ನ ಬಗ್ಗೆ 'about you', ಅದರ ಬಗ್ಗೆ 'about that'.

phrases.note: ಗುರು 'boss, man' and ಸಕ್ಕತ್ 'awesome' are for friends only.

phrases.en: Never mind, it's a long story. (informal)

grammar.title: Relative clauses: 'the film I saw', 'the man who came'
grammar.body:
Kannada has no word for 'who / which / that'. Instead, the verb of the describing clause becomes a **relative participle** and goes **before** the noun, like an adjective:
• **Past**: past stem + **-ಅ**: ಬಂದ 'who came', ನೋಡಿದ 'which (I) saw', ತಿಂದ 'which (we) ate', ಕೊಟ್ಟ 'which (you) gave'
• **Non-past**: stem + **-ಉವ** (spoken **-ಓ**): ಬರುವ / ಬರೋ 'who comes', ಮಾಡುವ / ಮಾಡೋ 'who does, where (I) work'
• **Negative**: stem + **-ಅದ**: ಬರದ 'who didn't come', ನೋಡದ 'which (I) haven't seen'

ನಿನ್ನೆ ಬಂದ ಹುಡುಗ 'the boy who came yesterday'
ನಾನು ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುವ ಕಂಪನಿ 'the company where I work'
ಅಮ್ಮ ಮಾಡಿದ ಅಡುಗೆ 'the food Mum made'

The participle never changes for the noun, and everything that belongs to the clause (subject, object, time) sits in front of it: [ನಿನ್ನೆ ನಾವು ನೋಡಿದ] ಸಿನಿಮಾ.

**'The one who / what'**: add a pronoun ending and the participle becomes a noun: ಬಂದವನು 'the man who came', ಬಂದವಳು 'the woman who came', ಬಂದವರು 'the people who came' (spoken ಬಂದೋರು), ಬರದವರು 'those who didn't come'. For things, add **-ದ್ದು** (past) or **-ಓದು** (non-past): ನಾನು ಹೇಳಿದ್ದು 'what I said', ನಡೆದಿದ್ದು 'what happened', ಅವನು ಮಾಡೋದು 'what he does'. These are everywhere in conversation: ಯಾರು ಹೇಳಿದ್ದು? 'who said so?', ಅದೇ ಅಲ್ವಾ ನಾನು ಹೇಳಿದ್ದು! 'that's exactly what I said!'

**The trap**: don't look for a word for 'who' or 'that'. ಯಾರು and ಏನು are only question words.

examples.native: ನಿನ್ನೆ ನಾವು ನೋಡಿದ ಸಿನಿಮಾ ತುಂಬಾ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿತ್ತು
examples.roman: ninne nāvu nōḍida sinimā tumbā chennāgittu
examples.en: The film we saw yesterday was really good.

examples.native: ಕನ್ನಡ ಮಾತಾಡೋ ಜನ ತುಂಬಾ ಖುಷಿ ಪಡ್ತಾರೆ
examples.roman: kannaḍa mātāḍō jana tumbā khuṣi paḍtāre
examples.en: People who speak Kannada are delighted (when you try).
Who are the people who didn't come to the party?
The house they live in is very big.

grammar.title: Reported speech with ಅಂತ and ಅಂತೆ
grammar.body:
Kannada reports speech by repeating the **original words** and adding **ಅಂತ** (written ಎಂದು) plus a verb of saying, asking or thinking. Literally 'he said, "I'll come tomorrow"':
• Statement: ಅವನು ನಾಳೆ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ 'he said he'd come tomorrow'
• Question (keep the -ಆ): ಊಟ ಆಯ್ತಾ ಅಂತ ಕೇಳಿದ್ರು 'they asked if I'd eaten'
• Order: ಬಾ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ್ರು 'they told me to come'
• Name: ಇದನ್ನ ಕನ್ನಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಏನು ಅಂತಾರೆ? 'what do you call this in Kannada?'

Because the words are quoted, ನಾನು inside the quote is the original speaker. In casual speech people also shift it: ಅವನು ನಾಳೆ ಬರ್ತಾನೆ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ. Both are fine.

For short reports use the verb **ಅನ್ನು** 'say' on its own: ಏನಂದ? 'what did he say?', ಹೌದು ಅಂದ್ಳು 'she said yes', ಸಾರಿ ಅಂದೆ 'I said sorry'. Spoken past forms: ಅಂದೆ, ಅಂದ, ಅಂದ್ಳು, ಅಂದ್ವಿ, ಅಂದ್ರಿ, ಅಂದ್ರು.

**Hearsay -ಅಂತೆ** is attached to the end of a sentence and means 'apparently / I've heard / they say'. It fuses with the last word: ಬರ್ತಾನೆ + ಅಂತೆ → **ಬರ್ತಾನಂತೆ**, ಆಯ್ತು + ಅಂತೆ → **ಆಯ್ತಂತೆ**, ಬರಲ್ಲ + ಅಂತೆ → **ಬರಲ್ವಂತೆ**, ರಜೆ + ಅಂತೆ → **ರಜೆಯಂತೆ**. It's the polite way to pass on gossip: you're only repeating what you heard.

examples.native: ಅಮ್ಮ ಬೇಗ ಮನೆಗೆ ಬಾ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದರು
examples.roman: amma bēga manege bā anta hēḷidaru
examples.en: Mum told me to come home early.

examples.native: ಅವನು ನನ್ನ ಹತ್ರ ದುಡ್ಡು ಇದೆಯಾ ಅಂತ ಕೇಳಿದ
examples.roman: avanu nanna hatra duḍḍu ideyā anta kēḷida
examples.en: He asked me if I had money.
Apparently the bank is closed tomorrow.

grammar.title: Telling it well: connectors, fillers and reactions
grammar.body:
**Telling it in order**: ಮೊದಲು 'first' → ಆಮೇಲೆ 'then' → ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ 'by then, meanwhile' → ಇದ್ದಕ್ಕಿದ್ದಂತೆ (spoken ಇದ್ದಕ್ಕಿದ್ದ ಹಾಗೆ) 'suddenly' → ಹೇಗೋ 'somehow' → ಕೊನೆಗೆ 'in the end'. Open with **ನಿನ್ನೆ ಏನಾಯ್ತು ಗೊತ್ತಾ?** 'you know what happened yesterday?'. Chain actions with the past participle (practised in unit 22): ಎದ್ದು, ತಿಂಡಿ ತಿಂದು, ಆಫೀಸಿಗೆ ಹೋದೆ 'I got up, had breakfast and went to the office'.

**Keeping the floor (fillers)**: ಅಂದ್ರೆ 'I mean' (rephrasing), ಏನಂದ್ರೆ 'the thing is' (explaining), ಗೊತ್ತಾ? 'you know?', ಅಲ್ವಾ? 'right?', ಮತ್ತೆ 'so...', ಏನ್ ಹೇಳ್ತಿದ್ದೆ? 'what was I saying?', ಅಂದಹಾಗೆ 'by the way' (new topic), ಒಟ್ಟಿನಲ್ಲಿ 'anyway, all in all' (wrapping up).

**Reacting**: a Kannada listener reacts every sentence or two; silence sounds bored. ಹೂಂ 'mm-hm', ಹೌದಾ? 'really?', ಆಮೇಲೆ? 'and then?', ಅಯ್ಯೋ! 'oh no!', ಪಾಪ 'poor thing', ನಿಜವಾಗಲೂ? 'seriously?', ತಮಾಷೆ ಮಾಡ್ತಿದ್ದೀಯಾ? 'are you kidding?', ನಂಬೋಕೆ ಆಗ್ತಿಲ್ಲ! 'I can't believe it!', ಸೂಪರ್! / ಸಕ್ಕತ್! 'awesome!'

**-ಓ 'some-'**: add -ಓ to a question word: ಯಾರೋ 'someone', ಏನೋ 'something', ಎಲ್ಲೋ 'somewhere', ಹೇಗೋ 'somehow', ಯಾವಾಗಲೋ 'sometime'.

**Idioms everyone uses**: ತಲೆ ತಿನ್ನು 'pester' (eat someone's head); ಕೈ ಕೊಡು 'let someone down' (give a hand); ತಲೆ ಕೆಡು 'go mad, be fed up'; ಹೊಟ್ಟೆ ಉರಿ 'jealousy' (stomach burning).

examples.native: ನಿನ್ನೆ ಏನಾಯ್ತು ಗೊತ್ತಾ? ಇದ್ದಕ್ಕಿದ್ದ ಹಾಗೆ ಕರೆಂಟ್ ಹೋಯ್ತು
examples.roman: ninne ēnāytu gottā? iddakkidda hāge kareṇṭ hōytu
examples.en: You know what happened yesterday? Suddenly the power went.
I got up, had breakfast and went to the office.
The thing is, I didn't have time, you know?
He let me down at the last minute.

dialogue.title: You know what happened yesterday?
dialogue.setting: Kavya and Nikhil, friends from college, catch up over filter coffee at a darshini in Jayanagar.

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಏನೂ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಹಾಗೇ. ಆದ್ರೆ ನಿನ್ನೆ ಏನಾಯ್ತು ಗೊತ್ತಾ?
lines.roman: ēnū illa, ellā hāgē. ādre ninne ēnāytu gottā?
lines.en: Nothing much, same as ever. But you know what happened yesterday?

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ನಮ್ಮ ಮ್ಯಾನೇಜರ್ ಎಂಟು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಮೀಟಿಂಗ್ ಇದೆ, ಬೇಗ ಬನ್ನಿ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ್ರು.
lines.roman: namma myānējar eṇṭu gaṇṭege mīṭiṅg ide, bēga banni anta hēḷidru.
lines.en: Our manager said there's a meeting at eight, come early.

lines.speaker: Kavya
lines.en: At eight?! Oh, you poor thing!

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಕೇಳು. ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಇದ್ದಕ್ಕಿದ್ದಂತೆ ಜೋರು ಮಳೆ ಬಂತು. ಬಸ್ ಸಿಗಲಿಲ್ಲ, ಆಟೋನೂ ಸಿಗಲಿಲ್ಲ.
lines.roman: kēḷu. beḷigge iddakkiddante jōru maḷe bantu. bas sigalilla, āṭōnū sigalilla.
lines.en: Listen. In the morning it suddenly started pouring. No bus, no auto either.

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಹೇಗೋ ಒಂಬತ್ತು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಆಫೀಸ್ ತಲುಪಿದೆ. ಮ್ಯಾನೇಜರ್ ಬೈತಾರೆ ಅಂತ ನನಗೆ ತುಂಬಾ ಭಯ ಆಗಿತ್ತು.
lines.roman: hēgō ombattu gaṇṭege āphīs talupide. myānējar baitāre anta nanage tumbā bhaya āgittu.
lines.en: Somehow I got to the office at nine. I was really scared the manager would tell me off.

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಇಲ್ಲ! ಮೀಟಿಂಗ್ ರದ್ದಾಗಿತ್ತಂತೆ. ಅವರೇ ಹತ್ತು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ ಬಂದ್ರು!
lines.roman: illa! mīṭiṅg raddāgittante. avarē hattu gaṇṭege bandru!
lines.en: No! Apparently the meeting had been cancelled. He himself turned up at ten!

lines.speaker: Kavya
lines.en: Are you kidding? I can't believe it!

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.native: ಅದೇ! ಒಟ್ಟಿನಲ್ಲಿ ನನ್ನ ಬೆಳಿಗ್ಗೆ ಪೂರ್ತಿ ವೇಸ್ಟ್ ಆಯ್ತು.
lines.roman: adē! oṭṭinalli nanna beḷigge pūrti vēsṭ āytu.
lines.en: Exactly! Anyway, my whole morning was wasted.

lines.speaker: Kavya
lines.native: ಅಂದಹಾಗೆ, ರೋಹಿತ್ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಿಯಾ ಮದುವೆ ಆಗ್ತಿದ್ದಾರಂತೆ, ಗೊತ್ತಾ?
lines.roman: andahāge, rōhit mattu priyā maduve āgtiddārante, gottā?
lines.en: By the way, apparently Rohit and Priya are getting married, did you know?

lines.speaker: Nikhil
lines.en: No way, man! Seriously? Who told you?

culture:
A good chat (**ಹರಟೆ**) is a social art in Karnataka: over by-two coffee at a darshini, at the ಕಟ್ಟೆ (the raised platform outside a house or under a tree where neighbours sit), or on the office tea break. The listener is expected to react all the time with **ಹೂಂ**, **ಹೌದಾ?**, **ಅಯ್ಯೋ!**, **ಆಮೇಲೆ?**; staying silent sounds as if you've stopped listening.

With friends your age, use **ನೀನು** and the bare verb (ಹೇಳು, ಕೇಳು, ಬಿಡು). Switch to **ನೀವು** (ಹೇಳಿ, ಕೇಳಿ, ಬಿಡಿ) with anyone older, a colleague you don't know well, or a friend's parents. When you pass on news about someone older, use the respectful plural even in gossip: ಮ್ಯಾನೇಜರ್ ಬೈದ್ರು, not ಬೈದ.

Bengaluru youth mix Kannada and English freely (ಸೂಪರ್, ಶಾಕ್, ಸೀರಿಯಸ್ಲಿ?) and have their own slang: **ಮಗಾ** and **ಗುರು** 'dude, man', **ಸಕ್ಕತ್** 'awesome', **ಬೊಂಬಾಟ್** 'fantastic', **ಚಿಂದಿ** 'superb'. ಮಗಾ is mostly between young men; ಗುರು is used by almost everyone. Keep all of these for friends. In Mysuru and Mangaluru the slang is milder, and in North Karnataka you'll hear a different accent and forms like ಐತಿ for ಇದೆ.

tip.title: Telling it in order
tip.body:
- **ಮೊದಲು** 'first' → **ಆಮೇಲೆ** 'then' → **ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ** 'by then' → **ಇದ್ದಕ್ಕಿದ್ದಂತೆ** 'suddenly' → **ಕೊನೆಗೆ** 'in the end'.
- **ಹೇಗೋ** 'somehow' gets you out of any mess: ಹೇಗೋ ಮನೆ ತಲುಪಿದೆ.
- Start a story with **ನಿನ್ನೆ ಏನಾಯ್ತು ಗೊತ್ತಾ?** 'you know what happened yesterday?'

sentences.en: Yesterday morning the power suddenly went off.

sentences.native: ಮೊದಲು ಬಸ್ ಸಿಗಲಿಲ್ಲ, ಆಮೇಲೆ ಮಳೆ ಬಂತು.
sentences.roman: modalu bas sigalilla, āmēle maḷe bantu.
sentences.en: First I couldn't get a bus, then it started raining.
In the end I came home by auto.

sentences.native: ನಾನು ಓಡಿ ಬಂದೆ, ಆದರೆ ಅಷ್ಟರಲ್ಲಿ ರೈಲು ಹೋಗಿತ್ತು.
sentences.roman: nānu ōḍi bande, ādare aṣṭaralli railu hōgittu.
sentences.en: I came running, but by then the train had gone.
Somehow I got to the office at ten.
Suddenly she started crying.

sentences.native: ಕೊನೆಗೆ ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಸರಿ ಆಯ್ತು, ಚಿಂತೆ ಮಾಡಬೇಡ.
sentences.roman: konege ellā sari āytu, chinte māḍabēḍa.
sentences.en: In the end it all worked out, don't worry.
What's the matter? Why are you upset?
So, what's new at the office?

sentences.native: ಅವನ ಕತೆ ಬಿಡು, ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ತಡ ಮಾಡ್ತಾನೆ.
sentences.roman: avana kate biḍu, yāvāgalū taḍa māḍtāne.
sentences.en: Forget about him, he's always late.

sentences.native: ಏನೂ ಇಲ್ಲ, ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಹಾಗೇ, ನಿನ್ನ ಸುದ್ದಿ ಏನು?
sentences.roman: ēnū illa, ellā hāgē, ninna suddi ēnu?
sentences.en: Nothing much, same as ever. What's your news?
What happened? Tell me from the start.

tip.title: React all the time
tip.body:
- Keep the story going: **ಹೂಂ** 'mm-hm', **ಹೌದಾ?** 'really?', **ಆಮೇಲೆ?** 'and then?'.
- Bad news: **ಅಯ್ಯೋ!** 'oh no!', **ಪಾಪ** 'poor thing'.
- Big news: **ನಿಜವಾಗಲೂ?** 'seriously?', **ನಂಬೋಕೆ ಆಗ್ತಿಲ್ಲ!** 'I can't believe it!', **ಶಾಕ್ ಆಯ್ತು** 'I was shocked'.
- Good news, with friends only: **ಸಕ್ಕತ್!**, **ಸೂಪರ್!**

sentences.en: Oh no, you lost your phone?
Poor thing, she's had a fever for three days.

sentences.native: ಅವನು ಕೆಲಸ ಬಿಟ್ಟ ಅಂತ ಕೇಳಿ ನನಗೆ ಶಾಕ್ ಆಯ್ತು.
sentences.roman: avanu kelasa biṭṭa anta kēḷi nanage shāk āytu.
sentences.en: I was shocked to hear he'd quit his job.
I believe you.
If I told you, you wouldn't believe it.
Seriously? The two of them are getting married?
Really? And then what did he do?

sentences.native: ಏನ್ ಗುರು, ನಿನ್ನ ಹೊಸ ಫೋನ್ ಸಕ್ಕತ್ತಾಗಿದೆ!
sentences.roman: ēn guru, ninna hosa phōn sakkattāgide!
sentences.en: Wow, man, your new phone is awesome!
Oh, poor thing, how is she now?
And then what happened? Did the police come?

sentences.roman: nambōke āgtilla, aidu varṣada nantara avanu phōn māḍida!
sentences.en: I can't believe it, he called after five years!

tip.title: Fillers that keep the chat going
tip.body:
- **ಅಂದ್ರೆ** 'I mean' rephrases; **ಏನಂದ್ರೆ** 'the thing is' starts an explanation.
- **ಗೊತ್ತಾ?** 'you know?' and **ಅಲ್ವಾ?** 'right?' go at the end and pull the listener in.
- **ಅಂದಹಾಗೆ** 'by the way' changes the topic; **ಒಟ್ಟಿನಲ್ಲಿ** 'anyway' wraps up.
- Lost the thread? **ಏನ್ ಹೇಳ್ತಿದ್ದೆ?**

sentences.native: ಏನಂದ್ರೆ, ನಿನ್ನೆ ನನಗೆ ತುಂಬಾ ಕೆಲಸ ಇತ್ತು.
sentences.roman: ēnandre, ninne nanage tumbā kelasa ittu.
sentences.en: The thing is, I had loads of work yesterday.

sentences.native: ನಾಳೆ ಸಿಗೋಣ, ಅಂದ್ರೆ ಸಂಜೆ ಆರು ಗಂಟೆಗೆ.
sentences.roman: nāḷe sigōṇa, andre sañje āru gaṇṭege.
sentences.en: Let's meet tomorrow, I mean at six in the evening.
So you mean you're not coming?
She's really nice, you know?
It's really humid today, isn't it?
By the way, how did your sister's exam go?
All in all, the party was awesome.
I was just asking, don't be upset.
Are you kidding? The exam is tomorrow?
I was only saying it as a joke!
Sorry, what was I saying?

tip.title: He said that…: quote + ಅಂತ
tip.body:
- Repeat the **actual words**, then add **ಅಂತ** + a verb of saying: ನಾಳೆ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ **ಅಂತ** ಹೇಳಿದ 'he said he'd come tomorrow'.
- Questions keep their **-ಆ**: ಊಟ ಆಯ್ತಾ ಅಂತ ಕೇಳಿದ್ರು.
- Orders stay orders: ಬಾ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ್ರು 'they told me to come'.
- Short reports use ಅನ್ನು: **ಏನಂದ?** 'what did he say?', **ಸಾರಿ ಅಂದ** 'he said sorry'.

sentences.en: The manager said tomorrow is a holiday.
Mum asked if I'd eaten.

sentences.native: ಅವನು ಐದು ನಿಮಿಷದಲ್ಲಿ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ.
sentences.roman: avanu aidu nimiṣadalli bartīni anta hēḷida.

tip.title: Apparently: -ಅಂತೆ
tip.body:
- Add **-ಅಂತೆ** to the end of a sentence to show you heard it from someone: ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತ**ಂತೆ** 'apparently it's going to rain'.
- It fuses with the last word: ಬರ್ತಾನೆ → **ಬರ್ತಾನಂತೆ**, ಆಯ್ತು → **ಆಯ್ತಂತೆ**, ಬರಲ್ಲ → **ಬರಲ್ವಂತೆ**, ರಜೆ → **ರಜೆಯಂತೆ**.
- Found out yourself? **ನನಗೆ ತಿಳೀತು** 'I came to know'.

sentences.en: Apparently it's going to pour in Bengaluru tomorrow.
Apparently Priya's got a new job.

sentences.native: ಅವರ ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಿನ್ನೆ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಗಲಾಟೆ ಆಯ್ತಂತೆ.
sentences.roman: avara maneyalli ninne doḍḍa galāṭe āytante.
sentences.en: Apparently there was a big row at their place yesterday.

sentences.en: We chatted for two hours over coffee.
Don't make noise, the baby's asleep.

lessons.title: The one who…, what I said

tip.title: The film I saw, the one who came
tip.body:
- No word for 'who / which': the verb becomes a participle **before** the noun: ನಿನ್ನೆ **ಬಂದ** ಹುಡುಗ 'the boy who came yesterday'.
- Past **-ಅ** (ಬಂದ, ನೋಡಿದ), non-past spoken **-ಓ** (ಬರೋ, ಮಾಡೋ), negative **-ಅದ** (ಬರದ).
- 'What (I) said' = **ಹೇಳಿದ್ದು**; 'those who came' = **ಬಂದವರು**.

sentences.en: Who was the girl who came to the party yesterday?
The book you gave me is really good.
